newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call spurts on late demand, gilt yields dip.
newsitem.headline: Indian call spurts on late demand, gilt yields dip.

text.p: Indian call money firmed up to end Thursday at 7.25-7.75 percent on late deamnd for funds, dealers said. Earlier, call money had slipped below five percent after opening in the 5.0-6.25 percent range, they said.

"Some banks left part of their positions open anticipating a fall in call rates in keeping with the trend of the last two days," a money market dealer at a state-run bank said. This led to some late demand for funds pushing up rates, he said.

Prices of government securities rose in the secondary market although trading volumes fell slightly, dealers said. Trade on the National Stock Exchange was 2.2 billion rupees on Thursday against Wednesday's 2.31 billion, they said.

The 13.50 percent 1997 stock was traded at a yield of 12.67 percent on Thursday against Wednesday's 12.83 percent while the zero-coupon 1999 was traded at 13.69 percent against 13.78 percent, dealers said.
"Some banks are taking positions anticipating a cut in cash reserve ratio and a fall in interest rates," a dealer said.
The Reserve Bank of India is expected to announce a cut in banks' cash reserve requirements later this month.
Dealers reported little activity in commecial papers and certificates of deposit. Rates on intercorporate deposits were steady in the 18-20 percent range for top-rated companies.
